Planned work: Pakenham and Cranbourne services start and end at Caulfield

9pm to last service each night, Monday 17 August to Wednesday 19 August  Note: Shuttle buses will operate North Melbourne to Parkville via Arden. To Metro Tunnel:  All Pakenham & Cranbourne Line trains will end at Caulfield. Take a Frankston line train to Melbourne Central to transfer to State Library. Take a Frankston line train to Flinders Street to transfer to Town Hall. To City:  All Pakenham & Cranbourne Line trains will end at Caulfield. Take a Frankston Line train to the City. From Metro Tunnel: All Pakenham & Cranbourne Line trains will start from Caulfield. If at State Library, go to Melbourne Central and take a Frankston Line train to Caulfield. If at Town Hall, go to Flinders Street and take a Frankston Line train to Caulfield. From City:  All Pakenham & Cranbourne Line trains will start from Caulfield. Take a Frankston Line train and change at Caulfield.

Planned work: Night works between North Melbourne and Newport

9pm to 4am each night, Monday 17 August to Wednesday 19 August  To improve the safety and efficiency of Melbourne’s metropolitan rail network, critical safety works will be undertaken along the Werribee and Williamstown lines. These critical safety works form part of Metro’s annual works program to maintain and renew the rail network.  What to expect:  medium to high level construction noise during the set up and use of the heavy machinery rail grinding works that will cause a short-term immediate increase in noise once completed, that will decrease over time increased noise, dust and local traffic in the works area or the rail corridor traffic management in place, as required.  Every effort will be made to carry out these works with respect for our valued neighbours. Works may be subject to change due to weather conditions and operational requirements.

Planned work: Mordialloc Station opening

First service Thursday 21 May From Thursday 21 May, your new station facilities include:  Lift and stair access to the new platforms, with entrances at each end of the station. A passenger waiting room, seating and toilets. A new ticketing office and myki machines. A section of car parking, including two accessible car spaces.  Finishing works will continue until late 2026.

Planned work: Trains are back at Boronia Station

First service Tuesday 4 August Trains are back at Boronia Station from Tuesday, 4 August Station entrance is via Erica Avenue. Passengers can access the platforms by using the lift or stairs. A new waiting room and myki facilities are also available at the station. Works will continue in the coming months. The Boronia Station upgrade will be complete in Spring 2026.

Planned work: Albion Station car park

Monday 2 February to late 2026 A new Albion Station will be built as part of Stage 1 of Melbourne Airport Rail and the Sunshine Superhub project. In order to complete major underground service relocation works, Albion Station car park will be closed. Alternative parking will be available at Tottenham Station on Rupert Street. Albion Station, access to platforms and drop off and pick up zones remain open during this time. Accessible car spaces Eight accessible car spaces at Albion Station will remain open. Shared use path closure A section of the shared use path will be closed at the southern end of the car park. Pedestrian and cyclist detours will be in place during this time.

Planned work: Watsonia Station car park changes

From April 2024 to 2028 The Watsonia Station car park has been closed since April 2024. From October 2025, there will be changes for pedestrians, cars, and buses accessing Watsonia Station as part of ongoing works for M80 Ring Road Completion.  new DDA-compliant paths and upgraded crossings to improve safety and accessibility for pedestrians. one-way entrance from Greensborough Highway northbound and a new signalised intersection for exiting vehicles. relocated bus stop and streamlined loop to support service reliability and reduce congestion.  These changes will be in place until a new Watsonia Station car park is built later in the project. We’re planning our work in the station precinct to minimise disruptions.  no changes to the pedestrian overpass or station platform access. maintaining accessible parking and drop-off and pick-up areas near the station entrance. providing more than 500 parking spaces at the nearby Watsonia Station commuter car park.
